title: Harness profile
description: How Aboard works with one harness: how to check it, start it, run it headless, resume it, give it an identity, install into it and deliver messages into its sessions. One file per harness, at adapters/<harness>/profile.yaml. aboard init, doctor, status and uninstall, the hooks, the delivery daemon and the launchers read it through one generic implementation; a harness's own Go package overrides only what the profile can't say. Command lines are argument vectors, never shell strings; {prompt}, {session}, {dir} and {bundle} are filled in when they run.

harness.description: The harness's name in Aboard: in ABOARD_SESSION, hook commands and the board file.

name.description: The name people know the harness by.

drives.description: real: this profile runs the tool itself. reimplementation: it runs something that imitates the tool (with its own settings, plugins, hooks or auth), which is a separate harness entry, never presented as the tool.

reimplements.description: For a reimplementation, the harness it imitates.

check_name.description: The short name aboard doctor gives this harness's checks and their codes: claude gives claude_hooks, claude_hooks_missing and claude_skill. The not-installed code is the harness's name with underscores, such as claude_code_not_installed. Default: the harness's name with underscores.

min_version.description: The oldest version of the harness Aboard works with, compared with the first version number its installed check prints. When the check prints no version, aboard init installs the hooks this version runs (see since). Read by the conformance kit.

sandbox_env.description: Variables the harness sets for commands it runs in its sandbox. A command that sees one doesn't start the delivery daemon, which would inherit the sandbox.

sandbox_network_env.description: The variables of sandbox_env the harness sets when its sandbox also blocks network access, local addresses and sockets included. A command that sees one and gets no answer from the server or the daemon fails with sandbox_blocks_network rather than saying they aren't running.

sandbox_fix.description: How the person gets the delivery daemon started outside the sandbox, completing "Either …, so its session-start hook starts the daemon outside the sandbox".

session_env.description: The markers: variables set in the environment of every command the agent runs in a session, by the harness or by Aboard's hooks. A command that sees one runs inside a session, so it refuses human actions such as changing the delivery mode. A marker another harness sets too (omp sets CLAUDECODE) is resolved with identity.precedence and identity.yields_to.

config_dir.description: The folder the harness reads its global config from (optional in the contract; every bundled profile declares it so a development sandbox can point the harness at a folder of its own): the folder the variable env names when it is set to an absolute path, else default under the home directory. {config_dir} in the install paths stands for it, so aboard init, doctor and status follow the variable.

login_files.description: Files in the config folder that hold the person's login for the harness, such as Codex's auth.json. A development sandbox (scripts/sandbox) links them from the person's own config folder into the sandbox's, so the harness there starts logged in; Aboard never reads them. Paths are relative to the config folder.

skills_dir.description: Deprecated: use install, with an item of kind skill. Where aboard init puts the Aboard skill for every project: under the home directory, or under the config folder when it starts with {config_dir}.

project.description: Deprecated: use install, whose items each name their project path. Where aboard init --scope project puts the skill and hooks, under the project directory. Hooks still run the installed aboard binary by absolute path.

allow_commands.description: Deprecated: use install, with an item of kind allow-rule. How aboard init --allow-commands lets the agent run aboard commands without a permission prompt, in the harness's own permission format.

rule.description: The allow rule, exactly as written.

file.description: The file that holds only this rule, relative to the harness's folder in each scope. Without it, the rule goes in the hooks file.

interactive.description: Starting an interactive session, for a terminal launcher such as tmux.

start.description: Starts a session with a first prompt. An element that is exactly {prompt} is the first prompt, and is left out when there is none.

resume.description: Opens an earlier session again by its id, {session}, in a terminal. {prompt} here is never the first prompt again, which the conversation already has: aboard swarm up gives a short note that the session was restarted, so its turn takes the messages that waited. aboard swarm up resumes an agent's last session with it; the live conformance kit too, with no prompt.

model.description: How to choose the model, {model}: put right after the program name in start and resume, followed by the board file's args.

launch.description: Where aboard swarm up puts a new session's identity. env (the default): ABOARD_AGENT and the launch ticket ABOARD_LAUNCH in the environment the launcher starts the harness with, for a harness whose hooks, extension or commands run in that process or its children. prompt: the first prompt's first line asks the agent to run aboard status --launch <ticket>, and the environment names no agent; the prompt hook hands the ticket in as the turn starts, and the command does when no hook runs. For a harness that runs its sessions and their commands in a long-running process it may share with sessions started elsewhere (Codex's app server), where the environment it was started with never reaches them, and could reach the person's other sessions.

headless.description: Running one turn without a terminal, for the headless runner. Each turn carries the agent's new messages as its prompt.

via.description: native: the harness's own non-interactive mode, with the commands below. acp: an Agent Client Protocol agent, started with acp.command.

run.description: Runs one turn and prints machine-readable output.

resume.description: Runs one turn in an earlier session.

session_from.description: Where the session id to resume is found in the run's output.

session_field.description: The key of the JSON object the run prints that holds the session id, which the headless launcher resumes with.

model.description: How to choose the model, {model}: put right after the program name in run and resume.

acp.description: The harness's Agent Client Protocol agent, if it has one.

package.description: Where to get the ACP agent.

env.description: Environment for the ACP agent; {command_path} is the harness's own program.

drives.description: Whether the ACP agent runs the real tool or reimplements it.

install.description: What aboard init installs, in this order, and aboard uninstall takes out again. Paths: global is under the home directory, or under the config folder when it starts with {config_dir}; project is under the project directory. Hook commands run the installed aboard binary by absolute path in both scopes.

identity.description: How a session knows which Aboard agent it is, and how a command finds the session it runs in.

session.description: How the CLI finds the session it runs in.

launched.description: How a launcher passes the agent's identity to a session it starts, so no join line is pasted.

kind.description: Where the session id comes from. env: a variable the harness sets in every command the agent runs (identity.env). hook: only the hooks' input; Aboard's session-start hook writes ABOARD_SESSION=<harness>:<id> and ABOARD_BOOT to the file that identity.env_file names, which the harness loads into every command. extension: Aboard's extension inside the harness sets ABOARD_SESSION itself.

env.description: For kind env, the variable that holds the session id.

root_env.description: For kind env, a variable that holds the root session's id in every command, set when a subagent's commands carry their own id in env (Codex's CODEX_SESSION_ID). A command whose two ids differ runs in a subagent.

env_file.description: For kind hook, the variable that names the session's environment file.

precedence.description: When the markers of several harnesses are set, the one with the highest precedence is checked first. Default 0; equal ones are checked in the registry's order.

yields_to.description: Variables that mean a command runs in another harness that sets or inherits this harness's markers. When one is set, the command isn't taken for this harness, and an ABOARD_SESSION or ABOARD_SUBAGENT naming it is ignored. Claude Code yields to OMPCODE, since omp sets CLAUDECODE as well, and to CODEX_THREAD_ID, since a Codex started inside a Claude Code session inherits its ABOARD_SESSION. For kind hook, the session-start hook writes unset into the environment file for each of these that is another harness's session variable (identity.env) and is set when it runs, since then it came from an outer session.

subagent_identity.description: Whether Aboard can tell a subagent's commands from its parent's. none: the harness has no subagents, or their commands can't be told apart, so a subagent may act as its parent; the harness's docs page states the risk. marked: they can (a hook of op mark-subagent marks them with ABOARD_SUBAGENT, the harness's extension does, or identity.root_env differs from identity.env), and a marked subagent may only read. seats: marked, and a subagent can be given a seat of its own. Default none.

lifecycle.description: How a session starts, ends and stays alive.

liveness.description: How the daemon knows a session is alive. process: its harness process is in the process table. connection: Aboard's extension inside the harness holds a connection to the daemon open.

outlives_terminal.description: True when sessions run in a long-running harness process with no terminal (Codex's app server), so quitting the terminal leaves the session open.

resume_keeps_id.description: True when resuming a session keeps its id, so the session-start hook binds it again to its agent.

resume_start.description: When a resumed session's start reaches Aboard. at-open: as it opens. first-turn: only once its first turn starts.

subagent_field.description: The hook-input field that is set when a hook fires inside a subagent. Such hooks take nothing: the messages belong to the root conversation.

delivery.description: How the delivery daemon puts messages into a session that is already open.

method.description: stop-hook: a hook waits while the session is idle and wakes it. queue: the harness's own queue takes the bundle. extension: Aboard's extension inside the harness receives bundles over its connection to the daemon. none: the agent runs aboard inbox --wait itself. delivery.capabilities says more.

capabilities.description: How messages reach a session, each a separate capability. idle-hook: a hook waits while the session is idle and wakes it with the bundle. turn-end-hook: a synchronous hook continues the turn with a fresh-checked bundle; queue wakes only idle sessions when this capability is active. queue: a command puts the bundle in the session's own queue, which starts it when the turn ends. tool-boundary: a hook adds the owner's messages to a running turn after a tool call. turn-start: the prompt hook (a hook of op prompt) or the extension adds, as a turn starts, the messages that waited quietly for it in focused mode. extension: Aboard's extension inside the harness holds a connection to the daemon, registers its session and process, receives bundles and confirms them. midturn-peer: the adapter can add eligible same-owner urgent direct messages to a running turn without interrupting it, only when the recipient policy permits; an extension must negotiate it live. none: the skill has the agent run aboard inbox --wait.

queue.description: For queue delivery, the command that queues a bundle.

hooks_file.description: Deprecated: use install, with an item of kind hooks. Where aboard init installs the hooks for every project: under the home directory, or under the config folder when it starts with {config_dir}.

event.description: The harness's name for the hook event.

op.description: What the hook does, in common terms. session-start: registers the session. prompt: a turn starts. wait: waits while the session is idle, and wakes it with a bundle. turn-end: the turn ended. tool: a tool boundary, where the owner's messages are added. end: the session closed. mark-subagent: before a command runs inside a subagent, marks it with ABOARD_SUBAGENT when it runs aboard; it never denies and never changes another command.

matcher.description: The harness's matcher for the hook's group, such as Bash for a hook that only sees shell commands. Without it, the group has no matcher and the hook fires for every tool.

timeout.description: The hook's timeout in seconds, written into its entry.

options.description: More settings of the hook's entry, in the harness's own words, written after its timeout: asyncRewake for Claude Code, additionalContextLimit for Codex.

since.description: The first version of the harness that runs this hook as written: it knows the event, and honors the hook's options and the output Aboard's hook gives. aboard init runs the harness's installed check and installs the hook when the version it prints is this one or later; otherwise it installs the fallback events that version knows, and nothing else. A version it can't read counts as checks.min_version, so aboard init never writes an event the installed harness may not know (Claude Code 1.0.23 to 2.1.100 ignore the whole settings file over one). Without since, every version gets the hook.

fallback.description: With since: the hook events that run the same command on older versions, each the event's name or {event, since} with the first version that knows it.

without.description: What the person loses on a version that runs neither the hook nor a fallback, as aboard doctor says it after "so": "an idle session doesn't wake for new messages".

mid_turn.description: tool-hook: a message from the agent's owner reaches a busy session at its next tool boundary, through a tool hook, or Aboard's extension inside the harness, that adds context. idle: it waits for the end of the turn like any other message.

waiting_notice.description: True when the tool hook also tells a busy session which other messages are waiting, by sequence number, sender name and sender label only.

notes.description: What was learned about the harness that the fields don't say.

json_true.description: A field of the JSON output that must be true; otherwise exit status 0 is enough.

kind.description: skill: the Aboard skill, a file Aboard owns. hooks: the delivery hooks, merged into a file shared with the person. file: a file inside the harness that Aboard owns, such as an extension, built into the binary. allow-rule: what aboard init --allow-commands adds so the agent runs aboard commands without a permission prompt. consent: a step the person takes before the harness uses what was installed.

global.description: Where the item goes for every project.

project.description: Where the item goes for this project only, under its directory.

format.description: For hooks, the shared file's format. json: {"hooks": {<event>: [{"hooks": [<entry>]}]}}, the other keys kept as they are.

source.description: For file, the name of the file built into aboard, under adapters/. aboard init writes this machine's aboard binary where the file says {aboard_binary} and the ABOARD_HOME it runs with where it says {aboard_home}, each as the inside of a JSON string.

rule.description: For allow-rule, the rule exactly as written. Without global and project paths, it goes in permissions.allow of the hooks file. With them, it goes in a file Aboard owns that holds only it, and counts as allowed in any file with the same extension in that folder, since the harness reads them all.

accepts.description: For allow-rule, other forms of the rule that already allow aboard.

note.description: For allow-rule, one line shown under the change, saying what the rule does in this harness.

required.description: For allow-rule, set when aboard commands can't reach Aboard from the harness without the rule (Codex's sandbox blocks network access): init recommends it, and doctor warns without it.

why.description: Why the rule is needed, in init's question.

advice.description: The line init adds when it sets the harness up without the rule.

missing.description: What init's overview says without the rule.

allowed.description: What doctor says with the rule, before the file that holds it.

not_allowed.description: What doctor says without the rule.

missing.description: For hooks, what doctor reports when they aren't installed. Without it, an error.

effect.description: What the person loses without the hooks, after a comma.

text.description: For consent, what the person does, completing "<harness> asks you to trust new hooks before they run: …".

project_text.description: For consent, one more line after a project setup.
